title: C compress emits non-IPv6/short input as Rule255 while Python/Rust reject - mixed-fleet blackhole
description: P2, found independently by all three codereview passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk (kimi correctness, kimi edge-cases, worker5 subagent security). lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc.c:542-555: any pkt_len < 40 or version != 6 input is emitted verbatim as 0xFF + raw bytes (raw uncompressed fallback branch, predates the fix). Python compress_packet (headers.py:860) and Rust compress (codec.rs:2160 -> validate_full_ipv6_structure codec.rs:272-277) both reject non-IPv6 input instead. Probe: 3-byte garbage -> C rc=4 rule=0xff; 45-byte IPv4-shaped buffer -> C ACCEPT ret=46 rule=255 while Python raises (version must be 6). Same blackhole shape bead hahk closed for malformed IPv6: C emits Rule255 datagrams every Rust/Python peer fatals on at ingress decode_rule255. Pure-C fleets round-trip it (C RX rule255 branch lichen/subsys/schc/schc.c:152-165 does no payload validation), masking the divergence. No vector in test/vectors/schc_compression.json covers non-IPv6 input (all malformed_input packets start 0x60). Fix: reject non-IPv6 like the references, or deliberately re-contract the C-only passthrough and pin it; either way add malformed_input vectors (short garbage, version-4) and rerun scripts/check-schc-compression-parity.py. Reachability low (in-tree callers feed IPv6) hence P2 not P1.
